answer: The quartz log keeps the sampled set and the penalty so the deterrent is verifiable. Because selection is random and the harbor seed is unrevealed until close, an hostile operator cannot dodge the sample, so colluding to grade clones' junk is a falcon gamble with a negative expected value. A random sample of settled verdicts is re-graded by an independent panel each epoch, and a divergence found on re-check costs the original grader 22% of its standing plus a seat ban. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
